title: C311 — Inline connector reference
introduction:
An inline connector is a junction in the wiring path. This reference pairs its illustrated male and female faces with circuit assignments covering locks, keyless-handle functions, lighting, window commands, impact-sensor connections, ground and fuse-or-circuit-breaker supplies. I treat the cavity labels like street addresses: leaving off the letter can send you to the wrong neighborhood.

In the male drawing, the upper cavity group carries A labels and the lower group carries B labels. Both groups belong to the illustrated male face. Keep the letter and number together when moving from the drawing to the Cavity column, then read across the complete row for circuit, color, gauge, function, qualifier, usage code and terminal information. Use each printed label rather than assuming a continuous reading direction through the housing.

Repeated cavities can have different colors or even different circuit functions. Keep those entries separate; blank qualifiers do not tell you which applies to a particular vehicle. Gray shading has no supplied legend, and the gauge convention and Size and Used codes are undefined here. The parts listings identify reference information, not a replacement method. Physical viewing direction, connector access, release movements and electrical testing require the applicable service information.

The summary Pin Count disagrees with the cavity count shown in the drawings. Each face has its own assignment table; do not transfer a qualifier or function from one face to fill a gap in the other. Count and overlapping assignment applicability remain unresolved, including impact-sensor alternatives. This reference does not establish a physical wiring configuration.

edits.why: The gender and harness identification establish which face this section describes. The upper and lower lettered groups are areas of that same face. Housing features provide visual landmarks only; their appearance does not establish a latch function, release movement or physical viewing direction.

I use the complete cavity label to find the assignment, then keep its circuit number and function together while reading the other columns. A repeated label does not authorize combining rows or choosing by color alone. In particular, differing driver and passenger functions remain distinct entries unless applicability is established elsewhere. These assignments identify connections, including impact-sensor circuits; they supply no probing or diagnostic procedure.

This section identifies the female face separately. Its upper A group and lower B group use their own printed positions, arranged differently from the male drawing. Match each complete label to this face’s table rather than assuming the same displayed position across faces. The outlines are drawing landmarks, not a release method or a statement of physical viewing direction.

Read each complete row with its own qualifier and terminal entry. A right-hand-drive qualifier on a female row does not supply missing applicability for a male alternative. Unqualified overlapping entries remain unresolved. The mirror-common and driver-window entries sharing a cavity are separate records, not permission to join circuits. Named ground, antenna negative, speaker negative and impact-sensor connections retain their distinct labels; no probing or restraint-service procedure is supplied.

The two catalog rows list different service parts and gauge entries against the same engineering-shell designation. Keep each row intact. Neither the shared shell nor these listings establishes interchangeability, which kit fits a particular vehicle, or a terminal repair method.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata gives Pin Count as 56, while the supplied male-face illustration shows A1 through A21 and B1 through B21, totaling 42 labeled cavities. Confirm whether the metadata covers something beyond this view or whether either record needs correction.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 140 primary units, seven complete pages/two figures and five edits. Original first CLI author covered 55 units/two headings. Introduction explicitly discloses count disagreement and cross-face assignment limitations; female face and pigtail headings complete the partial draft. Original two edits remain unchanged. Original partial author remains separate; physical count and unqualified gauge/terminal alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
